company: Cooper Energy Limited (subsequently renamed Amplitude Energy Limited, ASX: AEL)
title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel (KMP)
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the major activities of Cooper Energy, including directors and other senior executives identified in the most recent Annual Report as KMP.

tiers.name: CCPE
tiers.description: Closely Connected People and Entities of a KMP: close family members (spouses, minor children, dependent adult children) and any family company or trust that the KMP or close family member(s) control, significantly influence or have an interest in.

tiers.name: Other Designated Persons
tiers.description: Persons designated by the Board or by the Managing Director who may have access to inside information.

tiers.name: Other Employees
tiers.description: Personnel who are not KMP, CCPE of KMP, or an Other Designated Person; subject to a lighter notification-only regime.

tiers.name: Directors (other than Chairman)
tiers.description: Directors who are not the Chairman; distinguished only for clearance approver (the Chairman).

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of the Board; distinguished only for clearance approver (two other directors, or the Board).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board or the Managing Director may advise other Closed Periods from time to time (such as prior to announcement of a significant matter or event), and the Board has absolute discretion to vary any Closed Period or prohibit dealing in Cooper Energy Securities at any time, by written notice (including email); confidentiality of such a notice is not addressed.

rules.detail: Securities is expressly defined to include third-party financial products created in relation to Cooper Energy securities, including products which limit the economic risk of holding them, so an OTC put/call with a bank is a Security; Dealing broadly includes granting, accepting, exercising or discharging a right to acquire or dispose of securities. KMP, CCPE and Other Designated Persons need prior written consent under 6.1; all Personnel are barred during Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: financial products issued or created by third parties in relation to Cooper Energy securities (including products which limit the economic risk of holding securities in Cooper Energy).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, no clearance route, on hedging or transferring the risk of value fluctuation of unvested entitlements under any Cooper Energy equity-based incentive plan.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of any unvested entitlement (i.e., an entitlement that is subject to time and/or performance hurdles) in Cooper Energy Securities.

rules.detail: Hedging vested holdings is not itself banned; the pre-dealing consent confirmation only requires confirming the person is not hedging an unvested entitlement, implying vested-share hedging is dealt with under the ordinary consent process for KMP/CCPE/Other Designated Persons (or the Closed Period bar for Other Employees).
rules.evidence: that they are not hedging the risk of any fluctuation in value of any unvested entitlement in Cooper Energy Securities

rules.detail: A monetisation transferring the value-fluctuation risk of an unvested entitlement is caught by the same clause banning hedging of unvested entitlements.
rules.evidence: you must not enter into any transaction which would have the effect of hedging or otherwise transferring to any other person the risk of any fluctuation in the value of any unvested entitlement ... in Cooper Energy Securities.

rules.detail: Margin loans are expressly named and permitted only with prior written consent of the Chairman (or two other directors/the Board if the Chairman is the borrower), with mandatory disclosure of key terms, number of securities, trigger points, and the lender's unilateral right to sell.
rules.evidence: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Cooper Energy Securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan), unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman.

rules.detail: Granting security is not addressed as a standalone concept, but the 'Margin Loan' definition catches any financing arrangement carrying a risk that the Securities will be traded under its terms, and the Chairman must specifically be told 'the right of the lender to sell the Securities unilaterally' before consenting.
rules.evidence: the right of the lender to sell the Securities unilaterally

rules.detail: 'Margin Loan' is defined broadly to include 'other financing arrangement[s]' carrying a risk that the Securities will be traded under their terms, not just conventional margin loans, and requires the same prior written Chairman consent and Loan Information disclosure.
rules.evidence: or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Cooper Energy Securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan)

rules.detail: Short-term or speculative dealing is discouraged, not prohibited, and no clearance or notification specific to it is required beyond the general regime.
rules.evidence: Short term or speculative dealing in Cooper Energy Securities is not encouraged.

financing_disclosure: KMP (incl. Chairman), CCPE and Other Designated Persons: trigger = inception, before entering into the Margin Loan; to whom = the Chairman (or two other directors/the Board if the entering party is the Chairman); deadline = prior to entering into the arrangement; disclose key terms, number of Securities, trigger points, the lender's right to sell unilaterally, and any other material details.

exemption_authority: The Board has absolute discretion to vary a Closed Period or prohibit dealing at any time. During a Closed Period, the Chairman (or the Managing Director if the Chairman is involved) may grant written clearance to dispose of (not acquire) Securities for a fixed period of up to 2 business days, only in exceptional circumstances (hardship, an unforeseeable prior binding commitment, or other circumstances the Chairman deems exceptional) and only where disposal is the only reasonable course of action available.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You are not permitted to enter into a margin loan or other financing arrangement where there is a risk that Cooper Energy Securities will be traded pursuant to the terms of the margin loan or financing arrangement (together a Margin Loan), unless you have obtained prior written consent of the Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Although styled around 'Margin Loans', this sweeps in any financing arrangement carrying a risk that the pledged shares will be sold under its terms, so the bank's loan secured on the collared shares needs the Chairman's prior written consent regardless of how the facility is labelled.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the right of the lender to sell the Securities unilaterally
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Chairman must be told upfront that the bank has a unilateral enforcement right to sell the collared shares on default, and the policy gives no criteria constraining refusal, so consent is fully discretionary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If you are the Chairman and you intend to enter into a Margin Loan, you must obtain the prior written consent of two of the other directors or the Board to enter into the Margin Loan and disclose to those directors or the Board (as applicable) the Loan Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the Chairman is the executive seeking the collar financing, approval escalates to two other directors or the full Board rather than a single approver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: that they are not hedging the risk of any fluctuation in value of any unvested entitlement in Cooper Energy Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The standard pre-dealing confirmation for KMP/CCPE/Other Designated Persons only requires disclaiming hedging of unvested entitlements, supporting that a collar over vested shares is contemplated as permissible subject to ordinary consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Options in the Company may be exercised at any time in accordance with their terms of issue (including during a Closed Period) subject to the insider trading prohibition. Any subsequent sale of Securities issued on exercise of options will be subject to the terms of this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Vesting/exercise of underlying options is not itself blocked by a Closed Period, but the shares delivered on exercise (and any collar transaction over them) remain subject to the ordinary consent and Closed Period regime.

summary: A funded collar over vested shares is achievable under this policy, but every leg needs prior written consent because Securities are expressly defined to include third-party financial products that limit the economic risk of a holding, so an OTC put/call is squarely caught. For KMP, CCPE and Other Designated Persons, consent for the derivative legs comes from the Managing Director or Chairman (or two other directors if the Chairman is dealing), with post-trade notice to the Company Secretary within 2 business days; only unvested entitlements are absolutely barred from hedging or monetisation. The loan leg is separately and expressly regulated: any 'margin loan or other financing arrangement' carrying a risk that the shares will be traded under its terms needs the Chairman's prior written consent, with mandatory disclosure of key terms, trigger points, and specifically the lender's unilateral right to sell the shares — giving the Chairman full visibility (and discretion to refuse) before the facility is put in place. Outside Closed Periods (which run from 1 January/1 July until results are announced, and around the AGM) execution should be straightforward once consents are obtained; inside a Closed Period, only a disposal (not acquisition) can be cleared, and only for hardship, an unforeseeable prior commitment, or other Chairman-determined exceptional circumstances, for a maximum 2 business day window.
